entries.changed_by: human-guided (Ethan) -- explicit instruction, following a detailed frame/audio measurement analysis of a real published video (Portugal 1966 World Cup, ulVCT_wmFjY) against the same reference video used earlier
entries.diagnosis: Owner supplied a measured technical breakdown (shot timing, optical-flow motion, audio silence/noise-floor/stereo analysis, caption timing, brightness) of a real published video. Confirmed independently: the zoompan bug already fixed this session (0.00%/s measured motion on every shot, matching the diagnosis exactly, since this video predated that fix). New findings actioned here: captions ran slower/wrapped more than intended, AI images measured 24% mean brightness (moody/dark bias from the 'cinematic lighting' prompt suffix), narration had 6.4s of dead air across 13 gaps (18% of runtime, TTS's natural sentence-boundary pauses with no bed underneath), only 1 joke where the format calls for 2-4, and the sentence-loop technique was skipped entirely despite already being documented -- the last one escalated mid-session to a hard requirement per explicit instruction ('loop-technique encouragement must not be optional it be constant').
entries.evidence: Direct frame/audio measurements supplied by the owner. Verified DASH_CONNECTOR-style structural checks the same way: DANGLING_ENDING_WORDS correctly accepts a real dangling ending ('...some') and correctly rejects two real closed-sentence endings from actually-published videos ('...captain.', '...story.'). Did not implement SSML <break> tags for the dead-air fix -- Chirp3-HD's SSML tag support is inconsistently documented across Google's own sources as of this session and unverifiable locally, and a malformed/unsupported tag risks breaking narration synthesis entirely, a far worse failure than the pause issue itself; used ffmpeg's silenceremove filter on the already-synthesized audio instead, a stable, well-documented approach with no TTS-request risk.
changes: pipeline/assemble.py: WORDS_PER_CAPTION 2->1 (measured 0.76s/chunk against a healthy reference's 0.42s, and occasional 2-word chunks were line-wrapping at this font size -- both resolved by dropping to single words)

pipeline/ai_broll.py: STYLE_SUFFIX's 'cinematic lighting' -> 'bright natural lighting, vivid colors' -- the original wording measurably biased SDXL toward dark/moody output (24% mean brightness vs. a healthy reference's 54%)
pipeline/quality_gate.py: added MIN_JOKES=2 (only enforced once a script is long enough, >=8 beats, to plausibly fit multiple claim/evidence/joke cycles) after a real video shipped with just 1

pipeline/quality_gate.py: added DANGLING_ENDING_WORDS -- the ending beat's final word must be a genuine dangling connector (some/to/and/which/etc.), not a closed sentence, structurally enforcing the sentence-loop technique now that it's mandatory rather than optional
ROUTINE_INSTRUCTIONS.md: sentence-loop technique upgraded from 'optional, use when it fits' to 'mandatory, every video' per explicit instruction mid-session

pipeline/assemble.py: added _trim_long_pauses() -- runs the synthesized narration through ffmpeg's silenceremove (stop_periods=-1, stop_duration=0.25s, stop_threshold=-40dB) before any beat-duration/caption-timing math happens, capping every internal pause at ~0.25s instead of leaving TTS's natural (and sometimes long) sentence-boundary gaps untouched. Threshold chosen well below the narration's own measured noise floor (-57 to -60+ dBFS) to avoid misclassifying a quiet word as silence

pipeline/assemble.py: added _build_ambient_bed() -- three detuned low sine tones (80/121/163 Hz) with independent slow tremolo, filtered to a narrow low band and mixed in quietly under every video, unconditionally (not gated behind MUSIC_ENABLED, which is about actual music tracks specifically and is a distinct concept from this room-tone-style bed). Synthesized rather than sourced, same reasoning as the existing hook chirp/mascot chime -- zero licensing question, and deliberately non-rhythmic (independent, non-synchronized tremolo rates per tone) so it can't read as having a beat, matching what the reference video's own audio measurably lacked

pipeline/assemble.py: removed _add_hook_sound() (the two-tone chirp previously mixed under the very start of beat 0) entirely, per explicit follow-up instruction -- now that the sentence-loop technique is mandatory, that chirp would play right at the loop seam (ending audio -> hook audio) and audibly interrupt the 'one continuous sentence' illusion the whole technique depends on. The beat-0 visual zoom-punch (HOOK_ZOOM_END) is unaffected, it's a separate, purely visual pattern-interrupt with no audio component

Not verified with a real render or listen in this session (no ffmpeg/TTS credentials available locally) -- the silenceremove and ambient-bed filter chains are standard, well-documented ffmpeg constructs reasoned through carefully, but genuinely unheard. Recommend an actual listen on the next real upload specifically for pause length and whether the ambient bed is audible without being distracting
